_comment: ── BOUNDARY. Added 2026-09-06 with the eight-copy unification. Every one of these was ALLOWED by all eight pre-unification copies except the two marked otherwise: the inner predicates resolved paths, but the GATE that decided whether they ran was `repo in probe`, a substring test that a symlink or a `..` traversal walks straight past.

── AND THE OTHER DIRECTION, because a guard that over-denies teaches an agent to route around it. `{{sibling}}` is a directory whose NAME begins with a protected root and which is not inside it; the bare `startsWith` that one lane's Python copy had shipped denied it.

── A DANGLING LINK INTO A PROTECTED ROOT. Added 2026-09-29. `{{dangling}}` points at a path INSIDE the lane's repo that does not exist yet. Python's os.path.realpath follows it anyway; node's realpathSync throws on it, and the JS walk-up used to fall back to the link's own unresolved spelling, so `echo x > <link>` and `mkdir <link>` — which CREATE the target inside the repo — were allowed by every JS shim and denied by every Python one. Measured on the live brain lane before the fix, not only in the export (where the repo itself is absent).

── DATA IS NOT CODE. Only one lane's Python copy masked quoted strings and heredoc bodies; the other seven copies denied a `rg` search pattern that merely CONTAINED a mutator word. The escape hatches below it (`bash -c`, `bash <<EOF`) are covered by shell-c-* and shell-heredoc above.

── AND THE MASKER MUST HONOUR BASH'S ESCAPES. Found by a Judgment Day judge and MEASURED 2026-09-06: `echo \' && rm -rf <REPO>/x \'` contains no real quote as far as bash is concerned, so it runs the `rm` — but the masker read the escaped quote as a delimiter and blanked the whole command out of the text the deny regexes see. three lanes went DENY -> ALLOW (they had no masking before; porting that one lane's masker carried its bug), and that lane had been ALLOWing it all along. This is the levelling-down the unification exists to refuse, and no vector or mutant could see it.

── REDIRECT TARGETS ARE WRITE TARGETS, so they go through the same fail-closed predicate as a copy destination instead of each copy's own `t.startsWith(REPO)`. A relative target now resolves against the cwd rather than being blanket-denied.

── LANE-SCOPED EXEMPTION. The spent-worktree teardown exists only where it was already shipped. `lane_specific` exempts the vector from the cross-lane agreement check and makes the difference an assertion instead of an invisible drift; `expect_by_lane` says what each lane must do.

── DESTINATION, NOT PAYLOAD. Added 2026-09-09. A protected root cited as EVIDENCE inside a heredoc body that is not fed to a shell is DATA, exactly like the heredoc-prose vectors above — but until this fix, the gate that decides whether to even LOOK at the command scanned the raw, unstripped text, so the citation alone opened the gate and a `git commit`/`tee` whose real destination was never protected got denied anyway. Measured twice on 2026-09-09 by two different brainers: a `git commit` recording a decision, and a `tee`-style append to a decisions.md entry, each citing another lane's protected root as the evidence for the entry they were writing.

command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
cites {{repo}} as evidence
EOF
)"

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
cites {{repo}} as evidence
EOF
)"

tee -a note.md <<'EOF'
cites {{repo}} as evidence
EOF

cat >> {{repo}}/decisions.md <<'EOF'
a perfectly benign entry
EOF

_comment: ── WHEN CONTENT IS THE ONLY SIGNAL, THE MESSAGE MUST SAY SO. A citation that is NOT inside a heredoc — a single-line quoted argument — still cannot be told apart from a real destination, so it stays denied (the safe default), but the reason must say it is a content match it could not confirm, not assert a destination it never resolved. `content_only: true` asks the harness to check for that wording instead of the ordinary confident one.

── NOT EVERY HEREDOC BODY IS DATA. Found adversarially while reviewing the fix above, before it shipped: `xargs` runs its command once per LINE of its stdin, so a heredoc line fed to it is a real argument, not prose, and `patch`'s destination is the `+++ b/<path>` header INSIDE the diff it is fed. Treating every non-shell heredoc target as data (the naive form of the fix above) would have let both straight past the gate — this is the negative space that fix has to respect.

── PRESERVATION, NOT JUST CITATION. Added 2026-09-09, severity raised by a real incident: a product-lane brainer had 600 leads and a send-state.json existing in a SINGLE COPY inside a live worktree `hw done` was about to remove, tried to copy them OUT (read protected, write outside — exactly what a brainer may do), and the guard blocked it for naming the worktree's path. It got out only by building the source path from string pieces in python. Acceptance criterion 1 is really this: a brainer must be able to execute a PRESERVATION action, not merely cite evidence. `cp`/`rsync` already resolve destination correctly; these vectors prove it against the WORKTREES root specifically (not just the repo), including the multi-file shape (leads + send-state in one command) the real incident needed, and that the reverse direction (writing INTO the worktree) stays denied.

── THE MESSAGE MUST NAME THE DESTINATION IT DETECTED, NOT JUST THAT A ROOT WAS NAMED. Flagged by the brainer's own probe of the fix above: a redirect via `$HOME/projects/...` was correctly still denied (destination genuinely resolved, not merely string-matched), but the message read 'the command names a protected root' and 'the check keys on the literal name appearing in it' — describing a mechanism this branch no longer runs, and pointing a reader at a citation to search for instead of the destination that was actually resolved.

message_contains: does not key on the literal text

_comment: ── A PATH SEGMENT IS NOT AN INVOCATION. Measured 2026-09-10 with `cwd` inside a lane: `MUTATORS`'s `\w-` anchoring excludes `/` and `.`, so a path segment merely NAMED after a mutator (`bin/node`, `bin/python`, `tools/cp`, `rm.md`) satisfied the same boundary a real invocation does, and a read-only `ls`/`cat`/`test`/`wc` over such a path was denied. cwd is inside the repo so these exercise the `stands_in_protected` gate, the same axis the bug vectors used.

── AND THE POSITION CHECK ABOVE MUST NOT WIDEN WHAT IT DENIES. Every one of these IS a real invocation of the mutator/interpreter as the command being run, and must stay denied exactly as `MUTATORS`'s plain word-boundary test already caught it — a bare full-path interpreter, one reached through a pipe, `env`, a leading variable assignment, or a `&&` chain, and `xargs` running its argument once per stdin line.
